brand.title: IQVIA (Production)
brand.subtitle: Knowledge Check — Selling the IQVIA Clinical Trial Financial Suite

questions.question: According to the course, what are the four modules that make up the CTFS sales enablement training?
choices: Introduction to CTFS, Understanding Customer Personas, Analyzing Cost and Opportunity, and Utilizing the UVP Calculator
GrantPlan, Site Payments, Contracting, and Forecasting
Clinical Operations, Digital Transformation, IT Leadership, and Finance
Budgeting, Invoicing, Payment Processing, and Compliance
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly right—these four modules build from business context through persona understanding to value quantification.
questions.feedback_incorrect: While some of these options reference CTFS capabilities or customer roles, the course Road Map on Slide 4 specifies the four training modules you selected.

questions.question: Which two statistics does the course cite to demonstrate that clinical trial complexity is growing?
choices: 49% growth in trial sites and 60% increase in protocol amendments
60% growth in trial sites and 49% increase in protocol amendments
35% growth in trial sites and 70% increase in protocol amendments
49% increase in payment disputes and 60% increase in manual data entry
questions.feedback_correct: These specific statistics appear on Slide 6 and illustrate the growing operational burden that makes CTFS relevant.
questions.feedback_incorrect: While both numbers relate to trial complexity, the correct pairing is 49% for trial sites and 60% for protocol amendments. Check Slide 6 to confirm these metrics.

questions.question: What is Rachel's primary role and top priority in the customer organization?
choices: VP IT Clinical who prioritizes integration and governance
Clinical Operations Director who prioritizes execution and predictability
Digital Transformation Leader who prioritizes scalable digital innovation
Finance Director who prioritizes cost reduction across all departments
questions.feedback_correct: Rachel is the Clinical Operations Director focused on keeping studies moving and maintaining productive site relationships.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The course introduces three main personas—Rachel, Andrés, and Reena—each with distinct roles and priorities. Review Slide 16 to confirm Rachel's focus on execution and predictability.

questions.question: According to the course, which of the following best describes Andrés' view of CTFS value?
choices: He values CTFS primarily because it reduces manual invoice preparation for study teams.
He is interested in whether CTFS can produce measurable operational change at scale through agentic AI and extensible architecture.
He focuses on CTFS's ability to improve site relationship quality and reduce payment disputes.
He evaluates CTFS based on its compliance certifications and data security standards.
questions.feedback_correct: Andrés, the Digital Transformation Leader, is concerned with scalable digital innovation, agentic AI orchestration, APIs, and measurable transformation outcomes.
questions.feedback_incorrect: While each answer option reflects a valid CTFS benefit, Andrés's persona is specifically focused on digital transformation at scale. Review Slide 17 to understand his unique perspective on extensibility and AI.

questions.question: What does the course identify as the four main sources of customer impact when analyzing cost and opportunity?
choices: Software licensing fees, implementation costs, staff training, and ongoing support
Labor and administrative costs, delays and cycle-time costs, risk and compliance costs, and lost capacity and opportunity
Invoice processing, payment validation, forecasting, and budgeting
Clinical operations, digital transformation, IT infrastructure, and finance management
questions.feedback_correct: Slide 21 specifies these four sources of customer impact as the foundation for analyzing value during discovery.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The four sources of customer impact are not implementation costs or functional areas, but rather the business consequences of the current-state process. Review Slide 21 to understand how to quantify customer value.

questions.question: In the labor savings framework presented in the course, which elements are multiplied together to estimate annual labor savings?
choices: Process volume, average hourly rate, and number of process cycles per year
Hours saved per week, average hourly rate, number of employees, and the annualized working period
Manual effort hours, cost of tools, solution cost, and time to implement
Invoice volume, dispute frequency, payment aging, and staff utilization rate
questions.feedback_correct: The labor savings formula multiplies hours saved by hourly rate by number of employees involved, then scales to an annual period.
questions.feedback_incorrect: While process metrics are important for discovery, the labor savings formula specifically uses hours saved, hourly rate, number of employees, and the annualized working period. See Slide 31 for the exact calculation.

questions.question: According to the course's UVP value framework, what five categories of value should be considered when building a business case?
choices: Process improvement, staff reduction, technology ROI, risk mitigation, and strategic alignment
Revenue uplift, cost savings, time savings, risk or downtime reduction, and solution cost
Implementation cost, licensing fees, training investment, maintenance, and integration expenses
Labor hours, invoice volume, payment disputes, cycle time, and audit compliance
questions.feedback_correct: Slide 29 presents the complete value framework with these five categories, showing how CTFS delivers both financial and operational benefits.
questions.feedback_incorrect: While several of these categories relate to business value, the UVP value framework specifically includes revenue uplift, cost savings, time savings, risk/downtime reduction, and solution cost. Review Slide 29 to understand the complete picture.

questions.question: The course emphasizes that when presenting labor cost savings, a seller should focus on what rather than on general efficiency claims?
choices: The total number of employees who will be reassigned to other departments
The percentage reduction in overall IT system spending
Quantified activities such as specific hours, number of invoices, and documented follow-up effort
The timeline required to achieve the projected savings over the first three years
questions.feedback_correct: Slide 22 instructs sellers to quantify activities rather than using vague language, asking for specifics like invoice volumes and time per review.
questions.feedback_incorrect: To build credibility, focus on verifiable, quantified activities rather than general statements about efficiency. Review Slide 22 to learn how to gather the specific metrics that support labor savings claims.

questions.question: When using the UVP Calculator, the course advises sellers to separate which two types of input information to maintain credibility?
choices: Customer assumptions and vendor marketing claims
Current-state costs and future-state benefits
Facts from assumptions, and validate customer-provided metrics against labeled benchmarks
Financial impact and operational impact, keeping them in separate worksheets
questions.feedback_correct: Slide 27 emphasizes that credibility requires distinguishing verified customer data from assumptions and clearly labeling all benchmarks.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Credibility in value conversations comes from transparency about what is known, estimated, or still requiring validation. Review Slide 27 to understand how to maintain trust through honest labeling of calculation inputs.

questions.question: According to the course, a strong UVP message should include which of the following elements in sequence?
choices: Product features, pricing information, implementation timeline, and customer references
Target persona, customer problem, measurable outcome, relevant CTFS capability, and strategic benefit
Business metrics, cost savings calculation, time savings estimate, and risk mitigation value
Current-state process description, competitive analysis, recommended solution, and next steps
questions.feedback_correct: Slide 34 outlines this five-element structure as the foundation for a focused, customer-relevant UVP message.
questions.feedback_incorrect: A strong UVP is structured around the customer's perspective, not product features or pricing. Review Slide 34 to see how naming the persona, problem, outcome, capability, and strategic benefit creates a coherent message.
